title: Reduced rational homology of the proper interval in a product of finite chains
statement: Let $r\geq1$ and let $m=(m_1,\ldots,m_r)\in\mathbf N^r$ be nonzero. Order $[0,m]=\prod_{i=1}^r\{0,\ldots,m_i\}$ coordinatewise, and let $T_m=[0,m]\setminus\{0,m\}$. Define an augmented chain complex $A(m)$ of rational vector spaces [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] as follows. For $k\geq0$, its basis consists of strict chains $v_0<\cdots<v_k$ in $T_m$; $A(m)_{-1}=\mathbf Q$ on the empty chain, and $A(m)_k=0$ for $k<-1$. The differential for $k\geq1$ deletes one vertex with signs $\sum_{a=0}^k(-1)^a[v_0<\cdots<\widehat v_a<\cdots<v_k]$; the degree-zero differential sends every vertex to $1\in\mathbf Q$, and the degree $-1$ differential is zero. If at least one $m_i\geq2$, then $H_k(A(m))=0$ for every integer $k$. If every $m_i\in\{0,1\}$ and $s=\#\{i:m_i=1\}$, then $H_k(A(m))=0$ for $k\ne s-2$ and $\dim_{\mathbf Q}H_{s-2}(A(m))=1$. This includes $s=1$, when $T_m$ is empty and the nonzero homology is in degree $-1$.

proof.text: Use $C(P)=C(P;\mathbf Q)$ from [lem-sfb-poset-augmented-chain-prism]. The complex in the statement is precisely $C(T_m)$. Alternating deletion squares to zero: deleting positions $a<b$ in the two orders has coefficients $(-1)^{a+b-1}$ and $(-1)^{a+b}$; in degree one the two augmentations cancel. If monotone maps $f\leq g$ are compared by that lemma, then for a cycle $z$ one has $(g_*-f_*)z=d(hz)$, so they induce equal homology maps. If an induced map factors through the one-element poset $\{e\}$, its homology map is zero: $C(\{e\})$ is $\mathbf Q\xrightarrow{1}\mathbf Q$ in degrees $0,-1$ and zero elsewhere, so every cycle there is a boundary. These observations apply also in degree $-1$.

proof.text: Suppose $m_j\geq2$ and put $e=(0,\ldots,1,\ldots,0)$ with $1$ in coordinate $j$. This is a vertex of $T_m$. Define $u:T_m\to T_m$ by $u(v)_j=\max(v_j,1)$ and $u(v)_i=v_i$ for $i\ne j$. This is monotone and nonzero. If $u(v)=m$, then $\max(v_j,1)=m_j\geq2$ forces $v_j=m_j$; all other coordinates are also those of $m$, contradicting $v\ne m$. Thus $u$ stays in $T_m$. Pointwise $\mathrm{id}\leq u$ and $c_e\leq u$, where $c_e$ is the constant map at $e$. By [lem-sfb-poset-augmented-chain-prism], their induced maps on cycles differ by boundaries. Consequently $H_k(\mathrm{id})=H_k(u)=H_k(c_e)=0$, the last equality following from factorization through $\{e\}$ as in step 1. Hence all $H_k(A(m))$ vanish.

proof.text: Now every $m_i\in\{0,1\}$. Discarding the zero coordinates identifies $[0,m]$ with the inclusion poset of subsets of $E=\{i:m_i=1\}$, and identifies $T_m$ with $P_E=\{S:\varnothing\ne S\subsetneq E\}$. The induced bijection of chain bases respects deletion and the empty chain, hence is a chain isomorphism. Put $B_E=C(P_E)$. Induct on $s=|E|\geq1$. If $s=1$, $P_E$ is empty, so $B_E$ is $\mathbf Q$ in degree $-1$ only; its homology is exactly as asserted. Degrees below $-1$ always have zero homology by the definition of $H_k$ [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology].

proof.text: For $s\geq2$, choose $a\in E$, put $v=E\setminus\{a\}$, and let $D=P_E\setminus\{v\}$ with its induced order. The map $u:D\to D$, $S\mapsto S\cup\{a\}$, is well defined: if its value were $E$, then either $S=E$ or $S=v$, both excluded; its value contains $a$ and so cannot be $v$. It is monotone, $\mathrm{id}_D\leq u$, and $c_{\{a\}}\leq u$. The vertex $\{a\}$ belongs to $D$ also for $s=2$. Apply [lem-sfb-poset-augmented-chain-prism] and the singleton calculation of step 1: the identity on every $H_k(C(D))$ equals a map factoring through $C(\{\{a\}\})$ and is zero. Thus $C(D)$ is acyclic, including in degree $-1$.

proof.text: The inclusion of chain bases defines $C(D)\hookrightarrow B_E$, identity in degree $-1$. Let $V=B_E/C(D)$, degree by degree, with the induced differential. A basis of $V_n$ for $n\geq0$ consists of the chains containing $v$. Since $v$ is a maximal element of $P_E$, these are exactly $[S_0<\cdots<S_{n-1}<v]$, with $\varnothing\ne S_i\subsetneq v$; for $n=0$ this means $[v]$. Thus there are basis bijections $V_n\cong(B_v)_{n-1}$ for all $n$, where $B_v=C(P_v)$ and the empty chain corresponds to $[v]$. The spaces $V_{-1}$ and $(B_v)_{-2}$ are both zero. Deleting the final $v$ gives a chain in $D$, hence zero in $V$; every other deletion keeps its original sign. Therefore these bijections identify the differential of $V$ with that of $B_v$ shifted one degree (without a sign change). In particular cycles and boundaries correspond, and $H_n(V)\cong H_{n-1}(B_v)$ directly by the quotient definition [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology].

proof.text: The degreewise exact sequence $0\to C(D)\to B_E\to V\to0$ gives the segment $H_n(C(D))\to H_n(B_E)\to H_n(V)\to H_{n-1}(C(D))$ by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact]. To apply its cochain convention, replace a chain complex $K$ by the integer cochain complex $K^{-q}$; $H^q$ is then $H_{-q}$. The category is rational vector spaces, an abelian module category, and short exactness holds in each degree by the explicit quotient construction of step 5, including $0\to\mathbf Q\xrightarrow{1}\mathbf Q\to0$ in degree $-1$. Both outside homology groups vanish by step 4, so exactness makes $H_n(B_E)\to H_n(V)$ an isomorphism for every integer $n$.

proof.text: Since $|v|=s-1\geq1$, the inductive hypothesis gives $H_j(B_v)=0$ except at $j=s-3$, where it is one-dimensional over $\mathbf Q$. Steps 5 and 6 identify $H_n(B_E)$ with $H_{n-1}(B_v)$, so its only nonzero degree is $n=s-2$ and its dimension is one. This proves the induction and, through step 3, the Boolean clause for all nonzero $m$, including zero coordinates. Together with step 2 it proves every case of the statement.
